answer: Canonical work receipts. Give each authorized quartz assay, umber pigment analysis, or juniper sample identification a unique task ID with one fixed bounty. The verifier validates the result and atomically consumes that ID before paying. Repackaging one result under N accounts cannot increase its total payout. To earn N bounties, an attacker must process N distinct authorized samples and bear their labor and equipment costs. This assumes task IDs cannot be duplicated or minted by claimants; otherwise aliases can create new budgets.
